{
  "items": [
    {
      "formal_name": "rothNumberNat_le",
      "informal_name": "Roth Number Upper Bound: $ \\text{rothNumberNat}(N) \\leq N $",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ (N : ℕ), rothNumberNat N ≤ N",
      "informal_description": "For any natural number $ N $, the Roth number $ \\text{rothNumberNat}(N) $, which denotes the maximum size of a subset of $ \\{0, 1, \\ldots, N-1\\} $ containing no three distinct elements forming an arithmetic progression, satisfies $ \\text{rothNumberNat}(N) \\leq N $.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Combinatorics.Additive.AP.Three.Defs"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound_le_degBound",
      "informal_name": "Monotonicity of Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {k₁ k₂ : ℕ} {D₁ D₂ : ℕ → ℕ},\n  k₁ ≤ k₂ →\n    ∀ (n : ℕ),\n      (∀ i < n, D₁ i ≤ D₂ i) → ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound k₁ D₁ n ≤ ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound k₂ D₂ n",
      "informal_description": "For natural numbers $k_1 \\leq k_2$, functions $D_1, D_2 : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$ satisfying $D_1(i) \\leq D_2(i)$ for all $i < n$, and any $n \\in \\mathbb{N}$, the degree bound computed with parameters $k_1$ and $D_1$ at $n$ is less than or equal to the degree bound computed with parameters $k_2$ and $D_2$ at $n$, i.e., $\\text{degBound}(k_1, D_1, n) \\leq \\text{degBound}(k_2, D_2, n)$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.RingTheory.Spectrum.Prime.ChevalleyComplexity"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound",
      "informal_name": "Numerical Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem",
      "kind": "definition",
      "type": "ℕ → (ℕ → ℕ) → ℕ → ℕ",
      "informal_description": "A function that takes a natural number $n$, a function $f : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$, and another natural number $m$, returning a natural number used to establish well-founded recursion in the context of multivariate polynomials and Chevalley's theorem. It computes bounds by recursively applying $f$ to $n$ and decrementing $m$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.RingTheory.Spectrum.Prime.ChevalleyComplexity"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound",
      "informal_name": "Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem",
      "kind": "definition",
      "type": "ℕ → (ℕ → ℕ) → ℕ → ℕ",
      "informal_description": "A function that computes a degree bound for multivariate polynomials, taking a natural number $n$, a function $f : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$, and an element of the sum type $\\mathbb{N} \\oplus \\mathbb{N}$. For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly. This is used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem to establish well-founded recursion for multivariate polynomial constructions.",
      "path": "Mathlib.RingTheory.Spectrum.Prime.ChevalleyComplexity"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound_mono",
      "informal_name": "Monotonicity of Chevalley's Numerical Bound for Multivariate Polynomials",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {k₁ k₂ : ℕ} {D₁ D₂ : ℕ → ℕ},\n  k₁ ≤ k₂ →\n    ∀ (n : ℕ),\n      (∀ i < n, D₁ i ≤ D₂ i) → ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound k₁ D₁ n ≤ ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound k₂ D₂ n",
      "informal_description": "For natural numbers $k₁ ≤ k₂$ and functions $D₁, D₂ : ℕ → ℕ$ satisfying $D₁(i) ≤ D₂(i)$ for all $i < n$, the numerical bound function satisfies $\\text{numBound}(k₁, D₁, n) ≤ \\text{numBound}(k₂, D₂, n)$. This establishes monotonicity of the bound in the context of multivariate polynomials and Chevalley's theorem.",
      "path": "Mathlib.RingTheory.Spectrum.Prime.ChevalleyComplexity"
    }
  ]
}

items.informal_description: For any natural number $ N $, the Roth number $ \text{rothNumberNat}(N) $, which denotes the maximum size of a subset of $ \{0, 1, \ldots, N-1\} $ containing no three distinct elements forming an arithmetic progression, satisfies $ \text{rothNumberNat}(N) \leq N $.

items.informal_name: Monotonicity of Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.type:
∀ {k₁ k₂ : ℕ} {D₁ D₂ : ℕ → ℕ},
  k₁ ≤ k₂ →
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      (∀ i < n, D₁ i ≤ D₂ i) → ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound k₁ D₁ n ≤ ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.degBound k₂ D₂ n
items.informal_description: For natural numbers $k_1 \leq k_2$, functions $D_1, D_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfying $D_1(i) \leq D_2(i)$ for all $i < n$, and any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the degree bound computed with parameters $k_1$ and $D_1$ at $n$ is less than or equal to the degree bound computed with parameters $k_2$ and $D_2$ at $n$, i.e., $\text{degBound}(k_1, D_1, n) \leq \text{degBound}(k_2, D_2, n)$.

items.informal_name: Numerical Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.informal_description: A function that takes a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and another natural number $m$, returning a natural number used to establish well-founded recursion in the context of multivariate polynomials and Chevalley's theorem. It computes bounds by recursively applying $f$ to $n$ and decrementing $m$.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.informal_description: A function that computes a degree bound for multivariate polynomials, taking a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and an element of the sum type $\mathbb{N} \oplus \mathbb{N}$. For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly. This is used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem to establish well-founded recursion for multivariate polynomial constructions.

items.informal_name: Monotonicity of Chevalley's Numerical Bound for Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {k₁ k₂ : ℕ} {D₁ D₂ : ℕ → ℕ},
  k₁ ≤ k₂ →
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      (∀ i < n, D₁ i ≤ D₂ i) → ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound k₁ D₁ n ≤ ChevalleyThm.MvPolynomialC.numBound k₂ D₂ n
items.informal_description: For natural numbers $k₁ ≤ k₂$ and functions $D₁, D₂ : ℕ → ℕ$ satisfying $D₁(i) ≤ D₂(i)$ for all $i < n$, the numerical bound function satisfies $\text{numBound}(k₁, D₁, n) ≤ \text{numBound}(k₂, D₂, n)$. This establishes monotonicity of the bound in the context of multivariate polynomials and Chevalley's theorem.
